subject: PAGE directive
notes: Rule: 'Comment-text-1 may contain any character in the compile-time computer's coded character set except for control characters as specified in Clause 6, Reference format, rule 3b.' (cite.py --check 7.3.19.3 -> OK §7.3.19.3 1)); §6.1 3b 'The implementor shall specify any control characters that terminate a free-form line...' (cite.py --check 6.1 -> OK §6.1 b)). Permission half verified by probe out/probe/page-directive/p2.cob (free form): comment-text with TAB, Latin-1 letters, CJK, the ASCII punctuation set incl. backslash and < >, and a FORM FEED is accepted and the program runs (OK). Exclusion half: the excluded characters are the ones that TERMINATE a line, and the preprocessor splits lines at CR/LF, so a terminating control character cannot lie inside comment-text-1 by construction — nothing further to diagnose. Side note (not this row's defect): docs/CONFORMANCE.md has no §6.1 rule 3b determination naming the line-terminating control characters (the only control-character determination is A.1-115, line sequential files); that obligation belongs to the §6.1 row.
